# OSX Proxmox Next

> Open-source tool that creates macOS virtual machines on Proxmox VE 9 with one command. It runs a 6-step TUI wizard (or a scriptable CLI) on the Proxmox host, auto-detects Intel/AMD/Xeon CPUs, downloads OpenCore and the official Apple recovery image, generates a SMBIOS identity, and boots the macOS installer. Supports macOS Ventura 13, Sonoma 14, Sequoia 15, and Tahoe 26.

Install (run as root on a Proxmox 9 host):
`bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lucid-fabrics/osx-proxmox-next/main/install.sh)"`

Key facts:
- Commands installed: `osx-next` (TUI wizard), `osx-next-cli` (headless CLI, dry-run by default, `--execute` to apply)
- Works on Intel (including hybrid 12th gen+ and Xeon) and AMD host CPUs; CPU mode is auto-selected
- Recovery images come from Apple's osrecovery API; OpenCore EFI is built automatically (no plist editing)
- A mandatory dry run previews every `qm` command before anything is created
- Post-install: `osx-next-cli doctor --vmid <id>` health-checks the VM
- License: open source, repository at https://github.com/lucid-fabrics/osx-proxmox-next
- Intended for testing, lab use, and learning; users are responsible for complying with Apple licensing
